1.title: Turn off the entry power
1.say: Push the black power switch marked entry bedroom to off. Leave it off until the cover is back on.
placements: black power toggle marked entry bedroom → OFF position in grey metal power box, third switch down on left side in the video, pushed with fingertip
watch_for: if the hallway light still turns on, you pushed the wrong switch
if the toggle sits in the middle, push it fully to off until it clicks
1.check_yourself: It should look like the small black switch for entry bedroom resting in the off position inside the open grey box.
1.safety: Keep your fingers only on the plastic switch and off any metal around it.

2.title: Lift off the wall cover
2.say: Unscrew the four small screws in the white cover. Lift the cover straight off the wall.
placements: four small cover screws → out of corners of white double cover over two switches, in the video: top two and bottom two holes, removed with power drill
white double cover plate → off the wall into your hand, revealing two white switches behind, in the video: left of white door lock
watch_for: if the cover will not come off, a screw is still holding it
if paint sticks, wiggle gently or the cover can crack
2.check_yourself: It should look like two white switches sitting open on the wall with no cover.

3.title: Take out the old switch
3.say: Unscrew the top and bottom screws on the right white switch. Pull the switch out and cut its two black wires free.
placements: top and bottom mounting screws on right white switch → out of metal tabs at top and bottom of blue wall hole, in the video: right side of double hole, removed with small screwdriver
right white switch body → out of blue wall hole into your hand, leaving left white switch still mounted, in the video: right opening beside door trim
two black wires on back of old switch → cut free with cutters at the switch, leaving short black ends hanging from wall hole in the video
watch_for: if the switch will not pull out, a mounting screw is still tight
if you cut the wrong wires, you may cut wires for the left switch that stays
3.check_yourself: It should look like one white switch still on the left with an open hole and loose wires on the right.
3.safety: Confirm the power is dead with a tester before you touch any wire.

4.title: Join the green and bare wires
4.say: Hold the green wire from the new switch against the bare wire from the wall. Twist a yellow cap on tight to cover the bare ends.
placements: green wire from new white switch → twisted together with bare copper wire hanging from blue wall hole, in the video: lower right side of hole near door trim
small yellow twist cap → screwed clockwise by fingers over joined green and bare ends until tight with no copper showing in the video
watch_for: if you see bare copper below the cap, the cap is loose
if the cap falls off with a tug, twist the wires tighter and recap
4.check_yourself: It should look like a green wire and a bare wire joined under one yellow cap hanging down.
4.safety: Keep the joined bare ends away from the other wall wires while you work.

5.title: Join white wires and cap blue
5.say: Twist the white wire from the new switch into the white bundle from the wall. Screw a yellow cap on tight to cover the joined white ends. Push a yellow cap alone onto the short blue wire from the new switch.
placements: white wire from new white switch → twisted into bundle of white wires from back of blue wall hole, in the video: middle of hole under yellow cap. narration says red cap but frame shows yellow
small yellow twist cap → screwed clockwise by fingers over joined white ends until tight with no copper showing in the video
short blue wire from new white switch → capped alone with small yellow cap and left unused near wall opening in the video
watch_for: if white copper shows below the cap, unscrew and retwist tighter
if the blue wire is left open, it can touch other wires so it must stay capped
5.check_yourself: It should look like a bundle of white wires under one yellow cap and a lone blue wire closed with another yellow cap.
5.safety: Keep the power off until all the white ends are fully covered.

6.title: Join black and red switch wires
6.say: Twist the black wire from the new switch to one black wire from the wall. Twist the red wire from the new switch to the other black wall wire. Screw a yellow cap tight onto each joined pair.
placements: black wire from new white switch → twisted together with one black wire from blue wall hole, in the video: right side of hole hanging down
red wire from new white switch → twisted together with the other black wire from blue wall hole, in the video: middle of hole
two small yellow twist caps → screwed clockwise by fingers, one over each black pair until tight with no copper showing in the video
watch_for: if bare copper shows below a cap, the joint is loose and can spark
if the light will not turn on later, a cap may be loose so tug gently to test
6.check_yourself: It should look like the new switch hanging with its black and red wires each joined to a black wall wire under yellow caps.
6.safety: Keep the two joined pairs apart so the bare ends never touch each other.

7.title: Push in and screw new switch
7.say: Tuck the joined wires gently back into the hole in the wall. Push the new white switch into the right side of the hole. Tighten the top and bottom screws with a screwdriver or drill.
placements: joined wires with yellow caps → folded gently back into blue wall hole behind switches, in the video: pushed into right opening with fingers
new white switch body → into right side of double wall hole beside left old white switch, in the video: right opening next to door trim
top and bottom mounting screws on new switch → through metal tabs into box and tightened with power drill from right side of frame in the video
watch_for: if the switch will not sit flat, wires are bunched behind it so repack them
if the metal tabs pinch a wire, pull the switch out and move the wire clear
7.check_yourself: It should look like a new white switch mounted beside the old white switch in the open wall hole.
7.safety: Keep your fingers clear of the sharp metal edges around the switch tabs.

8.title: Put back the wall cover
8.say: Set the white double cover over both switches on the wall. Tighten the four small screws at the corners with a screwdriver.
placements: white double cover plate → over both left old switch and right new switch on wall, in the video: left of white door lock covering blue hole
four small cover screws → into top and bottom holes of cover and tightened with small screwdriver by hand, in the video: two at top and two at bottom
watch_for: if the cover cracks, the corner screws are too tight
if the small green light is hidden, the cover is upside down so turn it
8.check_yourself: It should look like a white double cover over the wall with both switches showing and a small green light on.
